summary: Karunesh Shukla worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy after studying under V. P. Upadhyaya. He held posts at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1973, 1991) and founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation (attested 1991).

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Bonn (PhD ~1991, Habilitation ~1999) and held professorial and dean positions at the University of Bern from 1999.

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Allahabad, Oxford (Jesus College, M.A. ~1909), and Lincoln's Inn (~1910). He later served as Tagore Professor of Law at Calcutta (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was an archaeologist and Indologist. He held positions with the Government of India as Officiating Government Epigraphist (~1930–1932), the Archaeological Survey of India as Deputy Director-General (1937–1944), and at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Indologist Kashinath Trimbak Telang studied under Narayan Mahadev Parmanand and earned degrees from Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. He served at Elphinstone College, as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and as vice-chancellor of Mumbai University (1892–1893).

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Arts & Science College (~1914–1945) and later as Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1945–1976).

Kate Crosby works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She held positions at St Peter's College, Oxford (attested 1996), Cardiff University (attested 2002), the Buddhist Institute (2003), and SOAS University of London as holder of the Seiyu Kiriyama post.

Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London in 2008 and held a post at Birkbeck, University of London, attested in 2010.
Katharina Sabernig is a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Vienna in 2017 and held an appointment at the Medical University of Vienna.

Katherine Anne Narraway is a researcher in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her Master of Arts degree at McGill University, where she was supervised by G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2008).

Katherine Anne Paul works in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. She completed doctoral studies under Gudrun Bühnemann, also studying with teachers including Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, having also studied with William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She earned an M.A. from the University of Chicago, completed her Ph.D. at McGill University (~1968–1978), and served as a professor at McGill University from around 1978.

Archaeologist and Indologist Kathleen D. Morrison studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley. She served as Assistant Professor of Anthropology at Northwestern University (~1993–1995) and held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

Kathleen Kenyon was an archaeologist who attended St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College, Oxford. She held academic posts at UCL Institute of Archaeology and the University of London (1948–1962), followed by St Hugh's College (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl specialized in religious studies and Indology. She held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, DePauw University, Lewis & Clark College (~1988–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017) as Associate Professor of Religion.

Kathleen Marie Higgins is a philosopher who joined the University of Texas at Austin as Professor of Philosophy (~1986). She also held visiting appointments at the Bellagio Center (1993), Australian National University (1997), and Canberra School of Music (1997).

Kathleen McDonald is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers including Tenzin Gyatso, Yeshe Thubten, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation with the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown is a scholar in Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Michigan in 2000, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Walter M. Spink.
